items.t: From 16S rDNA-seq count data to microbial interactions: A comprehensive benchmark of co-occurrence network inference methods.
items.ab: The study of the ecological interactions within microbial communities is crucial for gaining deeper insights into community ensemble and evolution, enabling targeted modification of the community's functionality. Many inference approaches have been developed to derive ecological associations. Here, we focus on co-occurrence computational methods, in which associations are inferred from metagenomic abundance data by measuring the statistical dependence between species counts across different sampled populations. The limitations in culture-based experiments have hindered the ability to assess these methods' validity, leading to scarce application in metagenomics studies. To provide a comprehensive assessment of network inference method performance, we benchmark 18 different computational approaches across a broad spectrum of experimental scenarios. We use synthetic 16S rDNA-seq count data generated from known underlying interaction networks, enabling systematic and controlled evaluation. The benchmark spans scenarios varying in numbers of species and samples, sample richness, sequencing depth, and interaction network structure. We evaluated the performance of the methods both in terms of accuracy of the inferred network, using various metrics from binary classification theory and metrics coming from network science, and in terms of computational burden. items.t: Explainable Protein Language Model Embeddings for Rapid Antibiotic Resistance Gene Classification
items.ab: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major public-health threat because resistant infections narrow therapeutic options, delay effective treatment, and increase the clinical and economic burden of bacterial disease. Conventional phenotypic susceptibility testing remains essential but requires 24–48 hours after isolate growth, while sequence-based interpretation requires curated databases and bioinformatics expertise. This paper presents ResiScan, an explainable machine-learning framework for rapid classification of antibiotic resistance genes from protein sequences. The proposed system uses the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD) protein homolog model data and extracts contextual protein representations with the pre-trained ESM2 model. Each protein sequence is tokenized, truncated to 512 residues for computational consistency, passed through ESM2, and represented by a 320-dimensional mean-pooled embedding. A logistic regression classifier is trained on these embeddings, with the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) applied only to the training partition to address severe class imbalance across five target resistance classes: beta-lactam, aminoglycoside, macrolide, tetracycline, and vancomycin. The framework further integrates SHAP-based feature attribution to expose which embedding dimensions contribute most strongly to each prediction, and provides an interactive Gradio web interface for non-specialist use. items.t: Experimental benchmarking of in silico annotations at prostate cancer risk loci and hypothesis-generating cross-cancer prioritisation of ovarian risk variants.
items.ab: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous non-coding risk variants for prostate and ovarian cancers, yet determining which are regulatorily active and which target genes they control remains challenging. We re-analysed a dinucleotide-barcode massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) of 208 bi-allelic prostate cancer risk single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in three prostate cancer cell lines under false-discovery-rate (FDR) control, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs at FDR < 0.10 (30 at FDR < 0.05), including 9 shared by at least two cell lines. Benchmarking standard in-silico functional annotations against this experimental ground truth revealed poor predictive performance (cross-validated ROC-AUC = 0.55-0.59), demonstrating that computational predictions cannot reliably substitute for measured allelic activity. We therefore treated the ovarian analysis as hypothesis-generating. Convergent annotation evidence prioritised 44 of 176 ovarian cancer GWAS leads (31 independent loci); a core of 21 SNPs (17 loci) was stable under alternative weights, leave-one-feature-out scoring and threshold changes, and candidates were enriched in ovarian and fallopian-tube regulatory chromatin (OR = 7.9, FDR = 5 × 10⁻5). items.t: Oxidation of Fe(II) by nitrate-reducing Fe(II)-oxidizers enriched from Fe(III)-rich microbial mats of an extreme acidic river (Río Tinto, Spain).
items.ab: Nitrate-reducing Fe(II)-oxidizing (NRFeOx) microorganisms have been detected in the subsurface of the Iberian Pyrite Belt (Spain), where the Río Tinto originates. However, it is not known whether NRFeOx microorganisms are present in the Fe(III)-rich microbial mats that developed within the surface waters where the river originates, and the geochemical conditions progressively shift from circumneutral to highly acidic. Moreover, it is not known what the main (microbial) Fe(II) oxidation pathway is under in situ pH conditions. items.t: Leaching Potential and Environmental Implications of Gold Ore Tailings From Ileki Ijesha, Osun State, Nigeria
items.ab: Abstract Gold mining in Nigeria, particularly artisanal and small-scale operations, generates large volumes of tailings that pose serious environmental and public health risks due to heavy metal leaching and potential acid mine drainage (AMD). This study assessed the leaching behavior and geochemical characteristics of gold ore tailings from Ileki Ijesha, Osun State, using batch and dynamic column leaching experiments. Five representative samples were analyzed for pH and concentrations of key metals (Fe, Mn, Pb, Cd, Zn, Cr, Ca) by Atomic Absorption Spectrometry. Leachates were further evaluated through PHREEQC geochemical modeling for speciation, saturation indices, and sensitivity analysis. Results revealed elevated iron (up to 22.2 mg/L) and manganese (up to 11.2 mg/L) concentrations, with moderate lead levels (6.6–7.81 mg/L) under near-neutral pH conditions (6.06–7.73). Modeling indicated supersaturation with iron (oxy) hydroxides and a critical pH threshold (~ 5.5) for accelerated metal release. These findings highlight significant long-term AMD risks and underscore the urgent need for improved tailings management and regulatory frameworks in Nigerian gold mining regions.

items.t: Rethinking the tumor microbiome: Methodological challenges and a framework for rigorous research.
items.ab: The intratumoral microbiome, as an essential component of the tumor microenvironment, has attracted increasing attention in recent years. The tumor microbiota displays an intricate interplay with its biological behaviors. However, emerging controversies, including the retraction of Poore et al.'s article, highlight significant challenges within this field. These issues extend beyond questions of reliability in this particular work to challenge fundamental theoretical assumptions and methodological validity across the entire field of tumor microbiome research, profoundly impacting its future direction. Here, we systematically summarize and discuss the current challenges and limitations in tumor microbiome research. We further propose a series of practical optimization strategies and solutions, from microbial quantification to functional experiments, providing a comprehensive framework covering the entire workflow of tumor microbiome analysis. With ongoing technical progress and standardized protocols, tumor microbiome research is poised to deliver novel insights into tumor biology and contribute to the development of improved therapeutic strategies.

items.t: Genomic and experimental evidence from Antarctic geothermal sites indicates diverse thermophiles are globally cosmopolitan
items.ab: Abstract Mt. Erebus, the world’s southernmost active volcano, is highly isolated, yet a previous study found its heated soils contain prokaryotes found elsewhere globally. This was unexpected, as non-sporulating thermophilic microorganisms are thought to be dispersal limited. We searched for the presence of metagenome assembled genomes (MAGs) from Antarctic geothermal sites outside Antarctica, finding that 62% of MAGs had matching species globally. Three of these cosmopolitan thermophiles isolated from Mt. Erebus could survive atmospheric-like conditions, with UV being the strongest selective pressure. Moreover, hot soils from Hawaiʻi sampled four years after a lava flow hosted many thermophilic MAGs with identical strains elsewhere globally, indicating that dispersal/recolonisation by thermophiles can be rapid. Finally, ice core sections from Fang Glacier (Mt. Erebus) associated with volcanic events were enriched in thermophiles, implying that thermophiles could disperse via volcanic events. Our findings dispel the common conception of thermophilic microorganisms as being inherently dispersal limited.

items.t: nannyrust: Rust Library for Dataset-Drift Detection and Label-Free Performance Estimation in Bioinformatics Machine-Learning Workflows
items.ab: Machine-learning models used in bioinformatics are exposed to covariate shift from new sequencing platforms, batches and cohorts, while ground-truth labels arrive late or never. We present nannyrust, a pure-Rust library with no third-party dependencies that implements univariate drift statistics (Kolmogorov–Smirnov, Wasserstein, Jensen–Shannon, Hellinger, chi-squared, L-infinity), classification metrics with ROC AUC, and confidence-based performance estimation (CBPE), so that monitoring can run inside compiled pipelines. Against SciPy and scikit-learn the core statistics agree to within 5 × 10⁻¹³ on 700 test datasets.

items.t: Metagenome-assembled genomes reveal Labilithrix thermalis sp. nov., an uncultured microorganism in hot springs.
items.ab: Geothermal environments harbor diverse microbial communities, including numerous phylogenetically novel lineages that remain largely unexplored. This study characterized two high quality metagenome assembled genomes (MAGs) from hot spring sediments in Yunnan Province, China. Phylogenetic analysis based on 16S rRNA gene sequences and genome sequences indicated that the two MAGs (JZ-3_bin_45TS and QQ_bin_234) should be assigned to the genus Labilithrix. Average nucleotide identity (ANI) and digital DNA-DNA hybridization (dDDH) values between the two MAGs and other genomes of the genus Labilithrix were below the recommended species thresholds (95% and 70%, respectively), indicating that the two MAGs represent a novel species within the genus Labilithrix. Genome annotation suggested an aerobic, chemoheterotrophic, and motile lifestyle, with the genetic potential for oxidative phosphorylation, tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, starch degradation, assimilatory sulfate reduction, arsenic detoxification, geothermal adaptation, and diverse biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs). Based on genomic and phylogenetic analysis, these MAGs should be classified as a novel species within this genus, for which the name Labilithrix thermalis sp. nov. is proposed following the rules of the published Code of Nomenclature of Prokaryotes Described from Sequence Data (SeqCode). items.t: Evolutionary histories of microbial calcification-associated genes across the tree of life.
items.ab: UNLABELLED: Biocalcification, a widespread process by which animals and algae form hard tissues and cellular structures, has played a major role in the global carbon cycle over the past 541 Ma. Extracellular or intracellular carbonates are formed by diverse bacteria, yet the genetic basis and evolutionary history of this process remain poorly resolved. Here, we present a large-scale survey of an intracellular calcification marker (calcyanin) and two calcification-associated genes with potential mineralization-promoting roles (carbonic anhydrase [CA] and urease) across the Bacteria and Archaea domains. High-sequence-coverage homologs of calcyanin are restricted to oxygenic cyanobacteria and consistent with vertical inheritance within seven families, suggesting a possible origin in a common ancestor of the Cyanobacteriia class, although some cases likely reflect horizontal gene transfer (HGT). In contrast, CA genes are widespread across all domains of life, with phylogenetic and structural analyses supporting independent origins of the α-, β-, and γ-classes, followed by extensive inter-phylum and possible inter-domain HGT events. items.t: Reducing acid mine drainage potential in sulfide-rich tailings through selective sulfide removal: A case study from a polymetallic mine deposit in northeastern Türkiye
items.ab: Abstract Sulfide-rich mine tailings represent a major source of acid mine drainage (AMD) and associated metal mobilization. This study evaluates selective pyrite flotation as a source-control strategy for reducing the acid-generation potential of flotation tailings from a polymetallic Pb-Zn mine. Pyrite-rich flotation tailings (PRT) and desulfurized flotation tailings (FLT) were characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and X-ray fluorescence (XRF), while their environmental behavior was assessed using short-term (72-h) contact leaching tests and acid-base accounting (ABA). Both tailings produced predominantly near-neutral leachates, with selective pyrite removal resulting in slightly higher pH values and generally lower mobility of several sulfide-associated elements. More importantly, total sulfur decreased from 10.6–14.7 wt.% in PRT to 0.8–1.8 wt.% in FLT, accompanied by a pronounced reduction in acid potential. Strongly negative net neutralization potential (NNP) values in PRT (− 299 to − 101 kg CaCO 3 /t) shifted to positive values in FLT (107.8–148.4 kg CaCO 3 /t), while neutralization potential ratios (NPR) increased from 0.35–0.69 to 2.95–6.82. XRD and XRF results further confirmed the reduction of sulfur-bearing phases following flotation. items.t: Systematic mapping of the prokaryotic noncoding sequence space with a genomic language model
items.ab: Prokaryotic genomes encode a vast repertoire of noncoding elements such as ribozymes, riboswitches, and CRISPR RNAs. The sequence-level diversity of these intergenic elements precludes alignment-based clustering that would enable annotation and discovery of novel noncoding RNA families. Here, we show that a genomic language model fine-tuned on prokaryotic intergenic sequences learns representations of noncoding elements from DNA sequence. We used these embeddings to organize 376 million intergenic regions from 1.3 terabase pairs of prokaryotic genomes and metagenomes into 5.14 million clusters. This approach nominated 20,149 clusters of putative structured RNAs with a candidate protein partner. Periodicity in token entropies revealed internal architecture, recovering CRISPR, TIGR and VIPR arrays together with their cognate effector proteins from sequence alone. Targeted clustering of bridge recombinase-adjacent sequences identified bridge RNA variants with longer guide recognition sequences than any characterized ortholog. Finally, we directed teams of AI agents to mine the database under researcher-defined criteria, uncovering divergent riboswitches, ribozymes, and other structured RNAs with biological hypotheses for their function. We release a publicly available database that transforms the dark matter of prokaryotic genomes into an explorable resource for human-agent molecular discovery.

items.t: Clinical pathogen adjudication in metagenomic sequencing using a large language model
items.ab: Clinical metagenomic sequencing detects hundreds of organisms whose relevance to infection requires clinicians' manual interpretation. We retrospectively reviewed 4,855 specimens from 19 sampling sites, linked 1.33 million detected organisms to clinical culprit-pathogen determinations, and fine-tuned a large language model on these labels. The model recovered 92.44% of reference culprit calls in the held-out test set and 84.49% in a later cohort. In a blinded re-adjudication of 215 cases, the model matched 90.5% of culprit calls on which both expert reviewers agreed. Adjudication accuracy varied with organism identity and specimen types. mNGS-derived metrics such as read counts or genome coverage alone were insufficient to identify culprit pathogens, and organisms classified as common colonizers could still be judged causative. Certain organisms were frequently co-reported as causative in the same specimen. These findings support further evaluation of human and AI-assisted report review, particularly regarding missed pathogens, excess calls, and differences across specimen types.

items.t: Engineering sticky microbes: A framework for appraisal of microbial cell-cell adhesion.
items.ab: Engineering bacterial consortia is key in biotechnological applications where specific spatial interactions among their components determine system performance. Genetic tools for programming cell-cell binding such as the nanobody-antigen (Nb-Ag; relying on non-covalent binding) and SpyCatcher-SpyTag (Spy; based on covalent linkage) systems are increasingly adopted as assets for enabling specific interactions of interest among otherwise detached members of a given combination of strains or species. Yet, despite the potential of these technologies, a robust metrology to quantify and compare the efficacy, stability, and specificity of inter-cell binding in a consortium is lacking. This work introduces a conceptual and experimental framework to systematically evaluate synthetic binding systems by combining aggregation assays, flow cytometry, and microscopy. Together, these techniques provide detailed insights into the structure and composition of engineered bacterial aggregates. This methodology was benchmarked with two Escherichia coli strains tagged with different fluorescent markers and engineered to surface-display matching adhesins. Under the test conditions, results showed that the Spy system outperformed the Nb-Ag system in terms of aggregation speed and stability. We also applied the same metrics for assessing the efficacy of the Spy system to mediate synthetic consortia of the opportunistic pathogenic bacterium Enterobacter cloacae. items.t: Seasonal and evolutionary patterns of planktonic Hikarchaeia reveal ecological niches of marine rare biosphere constituents.
items.ab: Members of Marine Group IV, now termed Hikarchaeia, hold an important transitional evolutionary position among Archaea but remain uncultivated, and their ecology remains uncharacterized. Over a 5-year period, we performed monthly profile sampling in the North Atlantic Subtropical Gyre and sequenced V4 16S rRNA gene amplicons, while also collecting additional size-fractionated and metagenomic samples. Hikarchaeal relative abundance annually peaked at ~1% of prokaryotic amplicons. Their relative abundances were significantly higher after deep winter mixing when thermal stratification isolated exported dissolved organic matter in the twilight zone (TZ), the boundary region between the epipelagic and mesopelagic. A diminutive 1.17 Mbp complete hikarchaeal genome was recovered by sequencing and co-assembling diel TZ metagenomes from 200 m during summer, where their relative abundances were highest. Phylogenomic reconstruction incorporating our new metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) and public MAGs established five clades. Clades I and III were in subtropical and tropical environments, with vertical partitioning: Clade I dominated the TZ, and Clade III detection initiated in the lower mesopelagic and extended into the bathypelagic. Clade V is polar-associated. Data sparsity makes Clade II and IV distributions unclear. All Hikarchaeia recovered thus far appear to be free-living aerobes capable of heterotrophy. items.t: A phyllosphere bacterium Exiguobacterium aurantiacum S11 mitigates cadmium toxicity in seagrass (Zostera marina) via a synergistic "exclusion-redox-repair" network.
items.ab: Heavy metal pollution, particularly cadmium (Cd), threatens coastal marine ecosystems and foundational species like the seagrass Zostera marina. Here, a multi-extremophilic phyllosphere bacterium, Exiguobacterium aurantiacum S11, was isolated to investigate its capacity and multi-dimensional molecular networks in mitigating acute Cd toxicity in Z. marina. In vitro assays confirmed high Cd tolerance in strain S11, driven by cell-surface biosorption and genomic active efflux systems (czcD, cadD, zupT, and znuA) regulated by cadC and resD. In an 18-day mesocosm challenge model utilizing 500 μM Cd, S11 inoculation reduced root Cd accumulation by 38.3% (p < 0.05) and attenuated systemic oxidative stress by suppressing malondialdehyde and stabilizing glutathione peroxidase activity. Furthermore, S11 specifically activated host folate biosynthesis, vitamin B6 metabolism, and DNA Base Excision Repair (BER) pathways, while promoting the accumulation of defensive diterpenes, flavonoids, and isoflavonoids. Overall, E. aurantiacum S11 establishes a synergistic "exclusion-redox-repair" network that enhances host resilience, offering a novel microbially assisted strategy for marine ecological restoration.

items.t: Annotation-Efficient Individual Muscle Segmentation from Dixon MRI: A Multi-Dataset Benchmark of Pretraining and Fat-Fraction Guidance.
items.ab: Measuring individual muscles and their fatty infiltration on Dixon MRI can support sarcopenia assessment, but manual annotation is time-consuming and annotated datasets are often small. This study investigated accurate individual-muscle segmentation with limited labelled data. Three datasets were used: an abdominal CT dataset of 300 subjects with adipose-tissue labels, a lower-limb Dixon MRI dataset of 25 subjects with 13 thigh and 9 calf muscles, and an independent cohort of 66 subjects for external testing. Network architecture, encoder pretraining, a Dixon-derived fat-fraction input, and a shared CT-MRI encoder were compared. A 2.5D model, subject-level cross-validation, zero-shot transfer, label-free domain adaptation, and few-shot adaptation were also evaluated. The best models reached Dice 0.947 ± 0.017 for CT adipose tissue and 0.925 ± 0.010 for thigh muscle; the best 2.5D model reached 0.928, while a reported 3D Attention-Res-V-Net reached 0.857 under a different protocol. Encoder pretraining helped most at the smallest budgets, with ImageNet performing best and comparably to CT-based pretraining at eight subjects. A shared CT-MRI encoder retained accuracy with 44 % fewer parameters, and thigh-muscle volumes agreed closely with reference measurements (ICC ( 2 , 1 ) = 0.998 ). items.t: Sulphate removal from synthetic acid mine drainage by iron-impregnated coconut shell biochar: role of iron retention and surface accessibility
items.ab: Abstract Acid mine drainage (AMD) carries high sulphate loads that lime neutralisation removes poorly. Iron-modified biochars are promising anion adsorbents, but the roles of iron loading and iron accessibility are rarely separated. In this study, coconut shell biochar produced at 650°C was impregnated with FeCl 3 ·6H 2 O at precursor-to-biochar mass ratios of 0.5, 0.7 and 1.0 g g − 1 (FeBC-0.5, FeBC-0.7 and FeBC-1.0). The materials were characterised by AAS, XRD and FTIR and tested for sulphate removal from synthetic AMD (initial sulphate 1958.6 mg L − 1 ; pH ≈ 2.5). The best material was then examined in a randomised factorial design with dose (2–6 g L − 1 ) and contact time (30–120 min) as factors. Iron retention levelled off above a ratio of 0.7, so FeBC-0.7 and FeBC-1.0 held the same total iron (13.90 and 13.88 mg g − 1 ). However, FeBC-0.7 showed the strongest Fe–O/Fe–OH absorption and removed more sulphate (90.2% versus 83.7% at 2 g L − 1 ). No crystalline iron oxide was detected, which indicates finely dispersed, X-ray-amorphous iron (oxyhydr)oxide. At 4 g L − 1 , FeBC-0.7 removed 90.93 ± 1.75% of sulphate, compared with 79.54 ± 1.08% for the pristine biochar, and reached 92.55 ± 0.32% at 60 min. items.ab: Abstract Secondary metabolites produced by Mycobacterium tuberculosis ( M. tuberculosis ) have been implicated in the hijacking of macrophage antibacterial responses through metabolic reprogramming that favors pathogen survival. items.t: Integrated 16S rRNA Bioinformatics Analysis of Gut Microbiota, Predicted Pathways, and Candidate Biomarkers in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
items.ab: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is associated with changes in gut microbiota composition and predicted microbial functions that may relate to intestinal immune processes. This study compared gut microbiota profiles between individuals with IBD and healthy controls and examined predicted microbial pathways and their associations with bacterial genera. Publicly available 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing data from 22 stool samples (11 IBD and 11 healthy controls) were analysed. Taxonomic profiling, diversity analysis, differential abundance testing, and PICRUSt2-based functional prediction were performed. Microbe–pathway associations were examined using Spearman correlation and Cytoscape. Extended analyses integrated differential abundance with machine-learning feature importance to prioritize candidate genera, evaluated a three-genus signature, assessed selected findings in an independent dataset, and compared predicted fermentation- and acetate-related pathways. Alpha diversity was significantly lower in the IBD group (Shannon index, p = 0.003), and Bray–Curtis PCoA showed separation of the two groups mainly along PC1 (PERMANOVA pseudo-F = 6.125, p < 0.001), although this separation may partly reflect differences between the source cohorts. items.t: An Enhanced Genomic Transformer for Multi-Dataset Forward-Validation Benchmarking in Pig Genomic Prediction.
items.ab: Genomic prediction models in pig breeding should forecast the performance of future selection candidates, yet random cross-validation does not accurately reflect this sequential setting. Here, we introduce an enhanced genomic transformer (EGT) that compresses genome-wide SNP profiles into compact tokens and incorporates a differentiable scoring term alongside mean squared error (MSE) during training. We constructed 70%/10%/20% forward-validation datasets for three pig datasets and evaluated single-trait and multi-task EGT variants against GBLUP, support-vector regression, random forest, XGBoost, CNN, and RNN across 12 prediction tasks. The better-performing EGT variant achieved a higher test-set Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) than the baseline for 10 of the 12 prediction tasks, with the largest improvement on LDL-C (+0.057). In BloodLipid ablations, autoencoder-only representation yielded the highest mean PCC (0.285), while Pearson-MSE objective reached 0.293 versus 0.291 for MSE-only training. Integrated-gradient analysis revealed a recurrent candidate region on Sus scrofa chromosome 13 across three lipid traits, and masking the top-attributed features reduced predictive performance more than a marker-count-matched random control for HDL-C, LDL-C and TG, whereas masking increased test-set PCC for TCHOL. This work establishes forward-validation benchmarks across three pig datasets and reports results to inform model selection and region prioritization in pig breeding.

items.t: Optimizing Pathogen Detection in Clinical Metagenomics: A Comprehensive Benchmarking of Bioinformatic Pipelines for Single-End Short Reads.
items.ab: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing for identifying pathogens has been increasingly used as a diagnostic tool. Prior research mostly emphasizes the selection of classification software based on reads above 100 bp, neglecting the influence of sequencing data preprocessing and post-processing stages. Independently, assessment was performed to assess the efficacy and effects of tools for each phase, encompassing quality control, host read elimination, taxonomic classification, and false positive removal, used in a metagenomics analysis pipeline employing single-end 50-bp reads derived from sequencing 13 positive-control mock community samples. The efficacy of tool combinations was assessed using single-end 50-bp data from identical mock samples processed using different wet-laboratory methods. The findings indicate that the selection of quality control and host-removal techniques is essential, significantly influencing the extraction of microbial reads from clinical metagenomic sequencing data and resulting in elevated α diversity. Although false-positive filtering enhances precision for trimming tool-based combinations without impacting recall, its effect is limited for combinations using the bt2 aligner. items.t: Type-Strain-Anchored Phylogenomics Reveals Taxonomic Discordance and Functional Variation in Agrobacterium.
items.ab: Species names deposited for Agrobacterium genomes do not always correspond to genomic lineages, complicating taxonomy and functional comparisons. We analyzed 432 genome records, including 400 assigned to Agrobacterium, using ANI, AAI, type-strain dDDH comparisons, and phylogenies based on 120 bacterial markers and 42 ribosomal proteins. ANI clustering at 95% identified 29 Agrobacterium groups, including five highlighted candidate species-level lineages. Both phylogenies supported a genus-level clade, although one ANI group showed discordance between the ribosomal-protein ML topology and bootstrap consensus. Type-strain dDDH supported conspecificity of A. fabacearum and A. tumefaciens (86.0%), whereas A. leguminum and A. deltae were below the conventional species boundary (66.7%). Pan-genome analysis of 31 representatives revealed extensive gene-content variation. Across 400 Agrobacterium records, 148 of 342 KEGG modules reached the reconstruction threshold in at least one genome, and 58 did so in all genomes. In the full 432-record dataset, 174 genomes had Ti-associated and seven had Ri-associated marker profiles; catB1 and tet(30) were detected in 243 and 29 genomes, respectively. These results identify taxonomic assignments requiring reassessment and link genomic grouping to variation in predicted functional repertoires.

items.t: Genome-Based Elucidation of Taxonomy, Pan-Genome Features and Secondary Metabolic Synthetic Capacity of Streptomyces griseorubens Strain MEPSL1 Isolated from Sweet Potato Roots
items.ab: Streptomyces griseorubens strain MEPSL1 is an endophytic actinomycetes isolated from sweet potato roots, with its 16S rRNA gene and genome sequence previously deposited in the NCBI database. To clarify both its taxonomic position and its strain-level biological significance, phylogenomic, comparative genomic and functional genome-mining analyses were performed. Using the Type Strain Genome Server (TYGS), digital DNA–DNA hybridization (dDDH) and phylogenetic analysis were performed to clarify its taxonomic status. The dDDH results showed that the d0 values between MEPSL1 and the type strains S. griseorubens JCM 4383 and DSM 40160 were 81.2% and 81.9%, respectively, both above the 70% prokaryotic species threshold, with G + C content differences below 1% and d4 similarity up to 91.6%, confirming MEPSL1 as Streptomyces griseorubens. Average nucleotide identity (ANI) analysis among 20 Streptomyces strains verified its generic affiliation. Pan-genome analysis revealed a typical open pan-genome with 19,872 pan-genes and 3056 core genes. COG annotation showed that metabolism-related genes were the most abundant, supporting its environmental adaptability and secondary metabolite biosynthesis potential. AntiSMASH predicted 24 secondary metabolite biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs), including four 100% identical to known clusters and seven putative novel clusters. items.t: Archaeal methanogenesis in a deep terrestrial aquifer driven by Methanothermobacter tomskensis sp. nov.
items.ab: Methanogenic archaea, capable of producing organic matter from hydrogen and CO2 emanating from the mantle, constitute one of the key functional groups of microorganisms in the deep subsurface. Although the diversity of methanogenic inhabitants of the deep biosphere has been studied in detail, the activity of methanogens in these biotopes remains virtually uncharacterized. We have measured the rate of hyrogenotrophic methanogenesis in water from the model borehole 3P (2.7 km deep), located near the small town of Parabel in the Tomsk Region. The potential rate of hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis, measured using 14C-labeled sodium bicarbonate, was 5.45 ± 0.528 nmol CH4/dm3/day (0.00545 ± 0.0005 nmol CH4/cm3/day) - a value compatible to the methanogenic archaeal activity known for anaerobic sediments of surface water bodies. The 16S rRNA gene profiles of water from well 3P were dominated by s single phylotype assigned to the genus Methanothermobacter; it accounted for 25.54% of the total microbial community. A MAG (metagenome assembled genome) designated 3P-20-051 and belonging to the genus Methanothermobacter was assembled from the water metagenome of well 3P. According to GTDB taxonomy, this MAG represents a novel species within the genus. The closest validly described relative of MAG 3P-20-001 was Methanothermobacter marburgensis with an ANI of 92.66%. items.t: Phylogenomic description of three novel species of the Microbulbifer genus, phylum Pseudomonadota, isolated from marine sponges and corals.
items.ab: Understudied bacterial genera present a dynamic phylogenetic landscape and opportunities for discovering new taxa as more strains are isolated and genomic data is added. Here, through phylogenomic analysis, we describe three novel species of the globally distributed cosmopolitan marine bacterial genus Microbulbifer. This genus is ubiquitous in marine microbiomes and is a validated source of biodegradation enzymes as well as high value small molecule natural products. Average nucleotide identity (ANI) to the closest known species, Microbulbifer variabilis ATCC 700307T, was less than 88.4% for all three novel species. Isolates of the three novel species, designated as PAAF003Ts (T = type genome), ZKSA006Ts, and SSSA003Ts were imaged to reveal their morphological characteristics. Based on phylogenetic data, strains PAAF003Ts, ZKSA006Ts, and SSSA003Ts represent three new species of the genus Microbulbifer, for which the names Microbulbifer maximicatervae sp. nov., Microbulbifer regidiadema sp. nov., and Microbulbifer mixtoriginis sp. nov. are proposed, respectively, under the SeqCode. We also reconstructed a robust phylogeny of available Microbulbifer genomes, which should facilitate future isolation and strain description studies.

items.t: Metagenomic insights into the pulmonary microbiome of drug-sensitive and multidrug-resistant tuberculosis patients.
items.ab: BACKGROUND: While the pulmonary microbiota may influence TB pathogenesis, direct comparisons between drug-sensitive (DS-TB) and multidrug-resistant (MDR-TB) patients remain scarce. This study explored microbiome differences between these groups. METHODS: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) from 30 prospective patients (11 DS-TB, 19 MDR-TB) was analysed via metagenomic sequencing. RESULTS: Patients with MDR-TB showed lower α-diversity and distinct β-diversity compared with patients with DS-TB. Streptococcus and Prevotella were relatively enriched in DS-TB, whereas Staphylococcus, Cutibacterium, and Mycobacterium were more abundant in MDR-TB. DS-TB showed enrichment of 45 carbohydrate-active enzyme families and core metabolic annotations, whereas MDR-TB showed enrichment of infection- and immunity-related functional annotations and a less connected taxonomic network. An exploratory random forest analysis identified six candidate genera and yielded an internally cross-validated AUC of 0.957. CONCLUSIONS: MDR-TB was associated with lower pulmonary microbial diversity, altered community composition, and shifts in predicted microbial functions. These findings characterise lower-airway microbiome differences between DS-TB and MDR-TB and provide a basis for further validation.

items.t: BiotaPredictor: A machine learning framework for predicting drug depletion by the human gut microbiota.
items.ab: The gut microbiota can profoundly influence the performance of oral medicines by metabolizing or bioaccumulating drugs, thereby reducing systemic exposure and contributing to variable patient responses. Despite growing recognition of these interactions, microbiota-driven drug depletion remains insufficiently addressed during early development. Here, we present BiotaPredictor, a freely accessible web-based machine learning platform that predicts the likelihood of drug depletion by human intestinal microbiota from molecular structure. We compiled two curated datasets containing microbial depletion outcomes: (i) a consistently annotated AstraZeneca dataset (158 compounds) and (ii) an expanded integrated dataset incorporating published evidence (522 compounds). Multiple molecular descriptors-including physicochemical properties, 3D conformational features, and fingerprint-based encodings-were evaluated across a suite of classification algorithms. A logistic regression model trained on the AstraZeneca dataset using physicochemical parameters achieved the highest performance, correctly classifying all compounds in an external validation study (3 depleted, 9 stable). BiotaPredictor enables early triage of compounds susceptible to microbiota-mediated loss and can inform lead optimization, formulation strategy, and pharmacokinetic prediction. items.t: Ecological partitioning and functional specialization of Thermoproteota across multiple trench sediments.
items.ab: Thermoproteota (formerly referred to as Thaumarchaeota) are phylogenetically divided into ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA) affiliated with Nitrososphaeria and basal non-ammonia-oxidizing archaea (non-AOA). While both groups co-existed in the hadal trenches, their differentiations across multiple trenches remain poorly understood. Here, 25 medium- and high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), including 18 AOA and 7 non-AOA representatives, were generated from metagenomics of Diamantina, Kermadec, Mariana-Yap trench sediments. AOA MAGs of Nitrosopumilales encompassing CSP1-1, DRGT01 and Nitrosopumilus exhibited chemoautotrophic potential with broader niche widths and higher diversity across trenches. Potential nitrification rates (PNR) were predominantly associated with AOA activity and exhibited clear depth-/trench-dependent patterns, driven by NH4+ availability. In contrast, the non-AOA lineage diverged approximately earlier (∼2.66 Ga), whereas the divergence between B1T1B5 and JAPUIC01 was estimated at ∼1.91 Ga during the Paleoproterozoic. B1T1B5 harbored auto/mixotrophic traits, whereas JAPUIC01 exhibited a metabolically flexible, heterotrophic strategy potentially suited to anaerobic niches. items.t: Shotgun metagenomic profiling of bacterial microbiomes, metagenome-assembled genomes and antimicrobial resistance in respiratory and blood samples from Gambian children with pneumonia
items.ab: Abstract Pneumonia is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in children, with bacterial pathogens being important etiologic agents. Most microbiome studies in pneumonia use technologies with limited taxonomical resolution and few include lung aspirate or blood samples. In this study, we assessed the microbial communities of the nasopharynx, nasopharynx/oropharynx, induced sputum, lung aspirate and blood, and recovered metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from the same sites using shotgun metagenomics sequencing of samples from children with severe and very severe pneumonia in The Gambia. Our data show that Proteobacteria and Firmicutes were the most common phyla across the body sites, and this was largely driven by S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae/aegyptius and M. catarrhalis. Blood and nasopharyngeal samples showed a mean Jaccard similarity of 58%, which was greater than expected under random pairing of specimens (q = 0.046). We recovered 60 medium-quality MAGs, of which 35 met the criteria for high-quality MAGs including 11 S. pneumoniae , 10 H. influenzae strains and a Limosilactobacillus with less than 95% Average Nucleotide Identity to the closest species in the Genome Taxonomy Database (GTDB). We also showed that antimicrobial resistance genes in our MAGs were highly species-specific; more than 70% of the unique AMR genes detected (11/15) were found only within MAGs of a single bacterial species rather than shared across multiple species. items.t: Linking microbial community reassembly to multi-element metabolic potential across community and genome scales in rivers impacted by ion-adsorption rare earth mining.
items.ab: Ion-adsorption rare earth element (REE) mining can create a composite pollution environment characterized by acidification and enrichment of NH4⁺, SO42⁻, and REEs, yet its effects on riverine microbial community assembly and multi-element metabolic potential remain poorly understood. Here, we combined 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, metagenomic sequencing, and metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) to characterize microbial community assembly and functional reorganization across a mining-disturbance gradient. At the community level, bacterial and archaeal richness and diversity declined significantly with increasing pollution, accompanied by clear community differentiation. Compared with bacteria, archaea exhibited greater environmental specificity, with larger contributions of homogeneous selection and dispersal limitation to community assembly. Meanwhile, microbial functional genes formed a modular network linking carbon, nitrogen, sulfur, iron, arsenic, and methane transformation processes, with particularly prominent cross-module associations among carbon-, nitrogen-, and sulfur-related functions. At the genome level, mining-associated MAGs showed multifunctional integration within individual genomes and potential functional division of labor and complementarity among different microbial members. items.t: Antioxidant-producing extremophile regulates gut microbiota of black soldier fly larvae to inhibit conjugative transfer mediated by plasmids in municipal sludge.
items.ab: Oxidative stress induced by heavy metals and antibiotics in municipal sludge inhibits the gut development of black soldier fly larvae (BSFL), compromising pollutant-processing capacity of their gut microbiota. Herein, Deinococcus radiodurans was colonized into the BSFL gut and established an antioxidant cascade regulatory system in concert with the gut microbiota, synergistically reducing the enrichment of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in municipal sludge. Results showed that bioaugmentation with Deinococcus radiodurans scavenges reactive oxygen species and upregulates the expression of G-protein and s14e genes in BSFL gut, maintaining normal gut function. On this basis, we propose two potential mechanisms responsible for inhibiting the horizontal transfer of ARGs (HGT). At the molecular level, bioaugmentation reduces environmental co-selection pressure through heavy metal immobilization mediated by extracellular polymeric substances and SlpA protein, as well as antibiotic degradation driven by gut microbiota, reducing the abundances of the class 1 integron integrase gene (intI1), conjugative transfer gene (traG), and ARGs (aphA and tetA) in municipal sludge by more than one order of magnitude. At the ecological level, bioaugmentation reshapes the microbial community structure of sludge, reducing the abundance of Pseudomonadota carrying mobile genetic elements and ARGs by approximately 26%. items.t: Chromosome-level genome assembly and annotation of the parthenogenetic nematode Acrobeloides nanus
items.ab: Acrobeloides nanus is a species of widely distributed bacteria-feeding nematodes belonging to the family Cephalobidae. It reproduces parthenogenetically, making it a valuable system for studying the consequences of obligate asexuality, and exhibits early developmental processes that differ significantly from the model organism Caenorhabditis elegans. Additionally, the species has demonstrated remarkable resistance in extreme conditions, surviving near-complete desiccation through anhydrobiosis. This new chromosome-level genome assembly provides a high-quality reference to study these traits. Combining Nanopore, amplified PacBio HiFi, and Hi-C sequencing, we generated a chromosome-level assembly spanning 188.9 Mb over six chromosomes. The genome features a 48.1% repeat content, dominated by Mutator-like elements, and contains 24,912 predicted genes. Structural analysis reveals the conservation of ancestral nematode linkage groups. This resource significantly improves upon previous fragmented assemblies, offering a new framework for identifying genomic adaptations in the family Cephalobidae.

items.t: Transcription factor CTCF activates KIAA1199 expression to inhibit ferroptosis and promote malignant behaviors in colorectal cancer based on bioinformatics and machine learning.

Cell type identification by estimating relative subsets of rna transcripts (CIBERSORT) was used for immune infiltration analysis. Tumor immune estimation resource (TIMER) database was used to assess gene expression across multiple cancers. Human transcription factor target database (hTFtarget) was used to predict regulatory relationships between genes and transcription factors. Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP), dual-luciferase assay, cell transfection, western blot (WB), and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) were used to detect protein-gene binding, transcriptional activity, gene knockdown and overexpression, protein expression, and mRNA expression. items.t: A hidden archaeal lineage with an ultra-reduced genome retaining only its replicative core.
items.ab: Host-associated prokaryotes can undergo extreme genome reduction, but the most reduced genomes belong to mutualistic endosymbionts whose hosts compensate for lost functions, eroding the symbiont's identity as an autonomous cell. Whether comparable reduction can occur while preserving the informational autonomy of a cell remains unclear. Here, we report the discovery of Candidatus Sukunaarchaeum mirabile, an archaeon with a genome of only 238 kbp (less than half the size of the smallest known archaeal genome) obtained by single-cell genomics from a dinoflagellate cell. Phylogenetic analyses reveal Sukunaarchaeum as an extremely divergent lineage that cannot be placed within any recognized archaeal phylum, although its precise branching position remains unresolved; environmental surveys indicate a diverse, geographically dispersed, and previously overlooked clade. Its genome lacks virtually all recognizable metabolic pathways yet retains the catalytic cores of the machinery for DNA replication, transcription, and translation, with losses largely confined to auxiliary and regulatory subunits. This profile contrasts with that of highly reduced mutualistic endosymbionts, in which informational genes are lost alongside metabolic ones, eroding autonomous cellular identity: Sukunaarchaeum encodes no recognizable metabolic pathway that could benefit a host, and instead dedicates ∼25% of its genome to large membrane proteins of unknown function, a feature paralleled by host-invasion pr

items.t: Physiological diversity and adaptation of Rhizaria revealed by phylogenomics and comparative transcriptomics.
items.ab: Protists are vastly diverse, forming over 20 supergroups of the eukaryotic diversity and fulfilling plentiful functions. Rhizaria is a widespread and highly abundant clade comprising important parasites and a huge diversity of free-living heterotrophic predators. Despite the diversity and biogeochemical importance of Rhizaria, our understanding of their physiology and metabolic capabilities remains limited, mainly due to limited genomic and transcriptomic data and methodological challenges associated with cross-species comparative transcriptome analyses. In this study, we assembled 15 transcriptomes of the bacterivorous Rhogostoma and their eukaryvorous relatives. By combining phylogenomic analyses and comparative analyses of population-level transcriptomes, we established an evolutionary framework to which we relate orthogroup similarity, orthogroup expression patterns, and functional annotations. The morphologically highly similar Rhogostoma strains formed two distinct phylogenetic clusters differing in orthogroups and orthogroup expression patterns related to cell adhesion and biofilm formation. Furthermore, we observed considerable intra-genus variation in amino acid and lipid metabolism in Rhogostoma, as well as lower completeness of these pathways compared to their eukaryvorous relatives. items.t: Strain handling exposes IS-mediated recurrent genome reduction at a dynamic accessory locus in Komagataeibacter rhaeticus
items.ab: Bacterial genomes are dynamic and harbour accessory regions that can be gained, lost, or rearranged in response to selective pressures. Members of the genus Komagataeibacter are used for bacterial cellulose production and researched as platforms for engineered living materials. However, their genomes are rich in mobile genetic elements (MGEs), including insertion sequences (ISs), genomic islands and prophage remnants, which drive genome rearrangements under agitated cultivation conditions. Whether this genome architecture contributes to genomic changes during routine strain maintenance and distribution remains poorly understood. Comparative genome sequencing of independent Komagataeibacter rhaeticus iGEM stocks revealed recurrent loss of a 210 kbp chromosomal region flanked by homologous IS5 sequences. This deletion was identified in a stock received as an agar stab and reproduced from an intact-genome population subjected to simulated agar-stab handling. Phylogenomic analysis of the affected locus revealed gene-tree/species-tree discordance, heterogeneous GC content and multiple ISs, supporting its characterization as a dynamic accessory region. Populations carrying the larger genome reduction showed improved growth and cellulose production relative to the intact genome reference, whereas populations carrying a smaller nested deletion showed reduced performance. items.t: Deep-sea siliceous sponges harbor distinct and functionally diverse microbiomes.
items.ab: Sponges, phylum Porifera, are long-lived and basal-branching metazoans that play important roles in ocean biogeochemistry and host diverse microbial communities. Siliceous sponges form a major clade of the Porifera; however, their microbiome is not well characterized, particularly in the deep ocean. Here, we used shotgun metagenomics to investigate the composition of the microbial communities of 13 siliceous sponges collected from four sites near Puerto Rico from depths ranging from 400 to 1,900 meters. Nine of the sponges in this study are from five sponge families that have not previously been sequenced using shotgun metagenomics. We assembled a total of 176 metagenome-assembled genomes from 20 bacterial phyla and 1 archaeal phylum. Ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA) Nitrosopumilaceae dominated most siliceous sponge microbial communities and was strikingly the sole symbiont associated with one sponge (Farrea). Overall, microbiome diversity was relatively low across siliceous sponges, except for a Phloeodictyidae, which is likely a high microbial abundance (HMA) sponge. Our results suggest that host sponge phylogeny may shape microbial community structure, with limited evidence for an environmental role. The sponge-associated microbial communities contained genetic capabilities for diverse metabolic functions, particularly contributing to the carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur cycles. items.t: Multi-response Optimization of Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans Cultivation for Enhanced Biomass Growth and Soluble Ferric Iron Production
items.ab: Abstract Optimizing the growth of Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans is essential for enhancing its efficiency in bioleaching and biomining applications. In this study, response surface methodology based on a central composite design was applied to evaluate the individual and interactive effects of pH, inoculum density, and ferrous sulphate concentration on growth kinetics and redox performance. Ferrous iron concentration and inoculum density were identified as the most influential factors, significantly affecting biomass production, specific growth rate, and ferric iron accumulation, whereas pH exerted a comparatively smaller effect within the investigated range. Significant interaction effects among the cultivation variables were observed, demonstrating the importance of considering factor interactions during process optimization. Multi-response optimization predicted that cultivation at pH 1.8, 10% inoculum, and 45 g/L FeSO₄ would support a specific growth rate of 0.053 h − 1 while maintaining elevated soluble ferric iron concentrations (8.497 g/L) within the tested range. Under these conditions, ferric iron remained comparatively stable in solution, indicating reduced ferric loss through precipitation. These findings highlight inoculum density as an important yet often overlooked cultivation parameter and demonstrate the value of statistically guided bioprocess optimization for improving A. ferrooxidans cultivation and ferric iron availability for bioleaching applications.

items.t: Dataset of amplicons, metagenomes, and metagenome-assembled genomes from geothermal biofilms four years after a volcanic eruption in Hawai'i.

Using the amplicon sequence data, we produced 276 ASVs from the universal primers and 576 ASVs from the archaeal-specific primers. Using the metagenome data, we reconstructed 82 medium-quality (>50% completeness and <10% contamination) and 61 high-quality (>90% completeness and <5% contamination) prokaryotic MAGs. Fastq files of the raw 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequences and metagenomes, as well as MAG sequences are publicly available on NCBI under BioProject PRJNA1459608. The amplicon sequence data indicated a strong effect of temperature, with communities dominated by Cyanobacteriota, Armatimonadota, and Pseudomonadota. The MAGs were primarily from domain Bacteria, having 142 MAGs, and 1 MAG from Archaea, with most abundance from phyla Chloroflexota, Proteobacteria and Acidobacteriota . items.t: Genomic potential for complete denitrification by Desulfobacillus in anammox bioreactors.
items.ab: Desulfobacillus are frequently observed as abundant flanking denitrifying microorganisms in anammox bioreactors and wastewater treatment systems. Previous studies suggested that Desulfobacillus lacked canonical nitric oxide reductase, restricting them to incomplete denitrification. As a result, they were thought to provide NO to anammox bacteria and act as an N2O sink. In this study, 48 Desulfobacillus genomes from GTDB were analyzed, including 21 from anammox-related bioreactors. Multiple potential nitric oxide reductases (eNOR, nNOR, and sNOR) were identified, and all 21 anammox-associated genomes encode at least one candidate nitric oxide reductase, with 5 also encoding a potential nitric oxide dismutase (NOD). The phylogeny, gene context, conserved active site residues, and 3D structures of these NO-transforming enzymes were further investigated. The findings indicated most Desulfobacillus possess the genomic potential for complete denitrification in anammox bioreactors. Furthermore, a discrepancy between 16S rRNA gene amplicon analysis and metagenomic analysis was observed. A proportion of Desulfobacillus 16S rRNA genes may be misclassified as Denitratisoma by the SILVA database. As Denitratisoma was previously detected in especially high abundance (>20%) in anammox bioreactors, this misclassification even highlights the importance of Desulfobacillus in anammox and other nitrogen removal processes.

items.t: Graded degradation of nucleotide second-messenger signaling and selective retention of structural metalloproteins in the Kryptonia phylum

items.t: PanGBank: a large-scale resource of precomputed microbial pangenomes built with PPanGGOLiN.
items.ab: PanGBank (https://pangbank.genoscope.cns.fr) is a comprehensive open-access database providing precomputed prokaryotic pangenomes at a broad taxonomic scale. Built upon PPanGGOLiN partitioned pangenome graphs, PanGBank addresses the growing need for large-scale comparative genomics through a standardized, regularly updated, and fully accessible resource. The initial release comprises two complementary collections covering >4600 prokaryotic species from the Genome Taxonomy Database (GTDB), encompassing over 393 000 genomes: GTDB_all, maximizing taxonomic and environmental diversity through the inclusion of metagenome-assembled genomes and single-cell amplified genomes, and GTDB_refseq, focusing on high-quality, annotation-rich genomes. Each species-level pangenome integrates graph-based statistical partitions into persistent, shell, and cloud gene families, together with regions of genomic plasticity (panRGP) and co-localized functional modules (panModule). PanGBank offers multiple access modes, including a REST API, a command-line interface, and an interactive web interface. By combining large-scale pangenome resources with advanced graph-based analyses, PanGBank provides a scalable framework for exploring microbial diversity, genome evolution, functional variation, and the dissemination of adaptive traits across prokaryotic populations, as illustrated by a use case on Acinetobacter baumannii pangenome investigating the distribution and evolution of antimicrobial resistance d

items.t: Uncovering novel phage defense systems through genomic island analysis in Streptococcus thermophilus
items.ab: Bacteria encode diverse antiviral defense systems, yet the evolutionary reservoirs that generate this immune innovation remain poorly defined. Although genomic context has been instrumental in discovering defense systems, genomic islands (GIs), variable chromosomal regions enriched in defense genes and proteins of unknown function, have not been systematically explored as sources of new bacterial immunity. Here, using comparative genomics of Streptococcus thermophilus, we identified 30 defense-associated GIs displaying extensive accessory gene diversity. Investigation of candidate loci from three GIs uncovered 15 previously uncharacterized antiviral systems, including 10 with novel architectures or features, revealing the potential within even a small subset of GIs. Several systems were not located near known defense genes, highlighting that GI-based discovery complements the traditional guilt-by-association approach, revealing systems that would otherwise remain undetected. Together, our findings establish GIs as reservoirs of antiviral innovation and provide a framework for uncovering the diversity of bacterial immune systems.

items.t: Comparative Genomics of Ecologically Differentiated Nitrososphaera-Related Ammonia-Oxidizing Archaea.
items.ab: Soil acidification strongly influences the ecology of terrestrial ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA). Within this group, the Nitrososphaera-related alpha (NS-α) and delta (NS-δ) lineages exhibit pronounced pH-associated ecological differentiation. In the preceding microcosm experiment, NS-α populations showed greater persistence than NS-δ during ammonium-driven soil acidification, yet the genomic basis underlying this ecological differentiation remains poorly understood. In this study, metagenomic sequencing of one near-neutral baseline microcosm (pH 7.35) and one acidified microcosm (pH 4.73) was used to reconstruct 12 Nitrososphaera-affiliated metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), including 2 NS-α and 10 NS-δ MAGs. These genomes were compared using genome-based phylogenetic analysis, amoA phylogeny, average amino acid identity (AAI), average nucleotide identity (ANI), and KEGG functional annotation to investigate lineage-level genomic differentiation and candidate functional genomic features. Genome-based phylogenetic and whole-genome similarity analyses supported clear differentiation between NS-α and NS-δ, while also revealing substantial genomic heterogeneity within NS-δ. Functions related to nitrogen acquisition and regulation, respiratory energy metabolism, autotrophic carbon fixation, and oxidative-stress defense were broadly distributed across both lineages and showed no clear NS-α-specific pattern. items.t: kamino: fast proteome-wide variant calling for amino acid phylogenomics.
items.ab: Amino acid-based phylogenetics usually relies on first clustering and aligning orthologous proteins. This approach is powerful but computationally demanding. Here, we present kamino, a reference- and alignment-free method that rapidly builds amino acid phylogenomic alignments directly from proteomes. As with similar algorithms, homologous regions are identified through shared sequences flanking variable regions. The method uses local changes in recoded k-mer occupancy to efficiently identify variable positions within these homologous regions and extract the corresponding pseudo-aligned sequences. It generates phylogenetically informative alignments across diverse prokaryotic and eukaryotic datasets. Phylogenetic analyses show that it accurately recovers Mycobacterium tuberculosis lineages, most curated GTDB taxa, and relationships consistent with published Drosophila and mammalian phylogenies, while producing signals broadly similar to BUSCO-based approaches. Runtimes are comparable to genome-based alignment-free methods and several orders of magnitude faster than classical marker-based pipelines, with moderate memory requirements. The method performs well across a broad range of divergence levels, from within-species comparisons to family-level prokaryotic and phylum-level eukaryotic datasets. kamino therefore provides a fast and simple route from proteomes to phylogenomic alignments across a broad range of evolutionary scales. items.t: Whole-Genome Sequencing Reveals the Resistome, Virulome, Pan-Genome Architecture, and Phylogenomic Diversity of Extensively Drug-Resistant Salmonella enterica Serovar Typhi in Pakistan.
items.ab: The emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi has severely constrained typhoid treatment. Pakistan is a major hotspot for XDR typhoid, yet genomic evidence defining the molecular basis of antimicrobial resistance, virulence, and genomic diversity of circulating strains remains limited. A cross-sectional study was conducted from January to December 2021 involving 252 culture-confirmed S. Typhi isolates collected from patients with suspected typhoid fever in Peshawar, Pakistan. Isolates were identified by conventional microbiological methods, biochemical testing, and 16S rRNA PCR. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) was performed according to CLSI guidelines, and isolates were classified as susceptible, MDR, or XDR following WHO criteria. Fourteen non-duplicate XDR isolates were selected for Illumina whole-genome sequencing (WGS). Bioinformatic analyses included genome assembly, multilocus sequence typing (MLST), resistome and virulome characterization, mutation analysis, pan-genome analysis, and core-genome phylogenetic reconstruction. Pearson's chi-square goodness-of-fit test was used to assess categorical distributions, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Among the 252 isolates, 152 (60.3%) were XDR, 73 (29.0%) were MDR, and 27 (10.7%) were susceptible. The distributions of sex, age group, and phenotypic classification differed significantly from equal expected proportions (p = 0.001,

items.t: Thermococcales pangenome uncovers new genera and modular evolution
items.ab: The order Thermococcales is unusual among Archaea in being known primarily from hundreds of lab-cultured isolates rather than metagenome-assembled genomes. Such cultivation is powerful for comparative genomics, allowing access to complete closed genomes rather than fragmented assemblies. We analysed 122 complete genomes, comprising all publicly available type species plus 67 new isolates, as a single pangenome. A combination of genome-scale metrics resolved 70 species across five genus-level clades, two proposed here as the new genera Oleococcus and Piezococcus , in addition to the canonical Pyrococcus, Palaeococcus, and Thermococcus. Only 6.1% of the 21,490 gene families are persistent, yet these contribute over half the genes in any genome. We observe that accessory functions, such as amino-acid biosynthesis, often behave modularly, being gained and lost as intact cassettes from genus-specific chromosomal loci. Combined with 114 mobile genetic elements, 72 integrated into the chromosome at conserved tRNA genes, and 42 extrachromosomal, we find that Thermococcales genomes accommodate rapid horizontal turnover through a constrained chromosomal architecture.

items.t: UShER-TB: scalable, comprehensive, accessible phylogenomic analysis of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
items.ab: Background. Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the bacterium responsible for tuberculosis, remains a leading cause of global infectious disease deaths. While genomic epidemiology is essential for understanding transmission dynamics and the rise of antibiotic resistance, significant computational limitations currently prevent comprehensive phylogenetic analysis of the vast number of publicly available M. tuberculosis genomes.Methods. We developed UShER-TB, a comprehensive collection of community resources, including a computational analysis pipeline designed for scalable phylogenomic analysis of M. tuberculosis. To demonstrate this system's utility, we processed 129,312 genomes to construct a global phylogeny. We evaluated the system's accuracy in transmission cluster reconstruction, its ability to identify novel genetic lineages and its performance in placing ancient DNA samples within the global tree.Results. The pipeline successfully constructed a global phylogeny capturing genomic diversity from over 129,000 samples. UShER-TB achieved high accuracy in reconstructing transmission clusters, reaching an adjusted Rand index of 0.95 when compared to conventional phylogenomic methods. This tool also facilitated the identification of putative novel lineages and sublineages. Furthermore, the platform enabled the successful phylogenetic placement of ancient samples. items.t: The bacterial antiphage protein Tiamat is an ATPase and DNase whose homologs are found across the tree of life.
items.ab: Bacteria and archaea encode hundreds of antiviral defense systems, some with homologs found in eukaryotic innate immunity. GHL ATPases like plant MORCs and prokaryotic Tiamat defend against viruses and phage, though their architecture and biochemical activities have remained unclear. Searching thousands of proteomes, we find Tiamat is rare in prokaryotes yet enriched across eukaryotes, including green plants, aquatic chordates, sponges, placozoans, and water molds. We resolve the central DUF3684 and flanking region into three predicted folds (TPR-like repeats, an uncharacterized conserved fold, and an inactive metalloprotease-like fold) that occupy the substrate-binding position of other GHL proteins. We show that purified Bacillus cereus Tiamat hydrolyzes ATP, inefficiently nicks duplex DNA, and cleaves single-stranded DNA site-specifically. We identify Tiamat-like proteins whose C-terminal nuclease is often swapped for helicases, peptidases, or other effectors. Additionally, we show Tiamat genes neighbor helicases, DNA methyltransferases, and nucleases, suggesting some Tiamats degrade foreign nucleic acid within a multi-component complex. Eukaryotic Tiamat homologs like the close Arabidopsis homolog NO VEIN and the distant human homolog SACSIN have acquired critical non-defense roles, leaving open whether these homologs remain antiviral or have been exapted.

items.t: Pangenome-resolved deconvolution of gut metatranscriptomes reveals species-specific microbial activity programs in Parkinson’s disease
items.ab: Abstract Gut microbiome alterations are associated with Parkinson’s disease (PD), yet their species-level functional consequences remain poorly understood. Here, we develop a pangenome-resolved framework integrating paired metagenomic and metatranscriptomic data to reconstruct species-level transcriptional profiles. Applied to two independent cohorts comprising 160 individuals and 7,548 profiles across 215 species, this approach revealed reduced genome-wide transcriptional breadth and increased inter-individual heterogeneity in PD. Genomic diversity and transcriptomic variation were significantly associated in 61 of 95 tested species. We identified 2,271 pangenome-resolved features associated with disease status, duration, or severity, with 39% of significant gene-level associations involving accessory genes. Species-specific responses included reduced metabolic and biosynthetic expression in commensals, including Coprococcus aceti and Streptococcus thermophilus, alongside increased stress-adaptation, mucin-degradation, and metal-homeostasis functions in other taxa. Cross-cohort classification performance varied substantially between species. These findings establish pangenome-resolved metatranscriptomics as a framework for identifying lineage-specific functional responses within microbiomes.

items.t: Pseudoalteromonas lipolytica and its EPS-overproducing variant for acid mine drainage control: biofilm formation and biomineralization.
items.ab: Acid mine drainage from metal sulfide tailings poses severe environmental risks. Although microbially induced carbonate precipitation (MICP) has been explored for heavy metal immobilization, the common ureolytic pathway generates harmful ammonia. This study demonstrated that Pseudoalteromonas lipolytica SCSIO 04301 and its extracellular polymeric substances (EPS)-overproducing variant effectively passivated pyrite and lead-zinc tailings via biomineralization without urea supplementation or ammonia release. Both strains formed biofilms and induced aragonite precipitation. For pyrite, passivation suppressed Fe release from ∼7500 μg/L to <60 μg/L over 180 days; leachates from passivated pyrite promoted Brassica chinensis growth to ∼100 mg fresh weight (vs. ∼53 mg for unpassivated controls). For tailings, both strains reduced total soluble metals (Fe + Al + Pb + Zn) to ≤45 μg/L, and leachates promoted plant growth to 93-121 mg. On pyrite, the EPS-overproducing variant formed a smoother, more uniform coating faster than the wild-type strain, which correlated with greater suppression of surface oxidation. On tailings, the wild-type strain formed large aggregates while the variant encapsulated individual particles; both achieved comparable passivation, but the variant showed higher susceptibility to heavy metal stress. Marine calcifying bacteria thus offer an environmentally benign alternative to ureolytic MICP for metal sulfide passivation, avoiding secondary ammonia pollution.

items.t: Williamsia profundi sp. nov., a novel deep-sea Actinomycetota isolate with versatile metabolic potential and specialized ecological adaptability.
items.ab: The deep-sea biosphere hosts distinctive microbial communities with specialized adaptive traits, yet the mechanisms underpinning their physiological survival remain largely obscure. In this study a novel Gram-stain-positive, aerobic bacterium, designated strain SKLECPSW1T, was isolated from the Eastern Indian Ocean at a depth of 5318 m. The strain grows optimally at 32 °C and has a DNA G + C content of 70.0 mol%. Its major fatty acids are C16:0, C18:1 ω9c, and 10-methyl-C18:0. Genome analysis revealed a versatile metabolic repertoire, including complete central carbon metabolic pathways, dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA), anaplerotic CO₂ fixation, and multiple genes associated with environmental stress responses. Furthermore, CAZyme profiling and 12 putative biosynthetic regions suggested potential for complex carbohydrate processing and secondary-metabolite biosynthesis. Comparative 16S rRNA gene sequence analysis showed that strain SKLECPSW1T shared the highest sequence similarity with Williamsia aurantiaca B375T (98.3%). Average Nucleotide Identity (ANI) and digital DNA-DNA hybridization (dDDH) values with related Williamsia species ranged from 71.15% to 83.35% and 18.8% to 26.6%, respectively, supporting its novel status. Metagenomic analysis of 25 deep-ocean datasets showed broad high-identity genome-wide recruitment in 2 samples, with breadths of 45.60% and 34.64% at ≥95% nucleotide identity, remaining 42.76% and 34.09% at ≥97.5%. items.t: Microbiologically influenced corrosion in extreme environments caused by problematic microbial biofilms.
items.ab: Microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) caused by microbial biofilms poses significant challenges to industrial systems. MIC and MIC mitigation cost billions of dollars each year in the US alone. Although most microbes flourish under mild conditions, increasing evidence demonstrates that in extreme environments such as high temperature, pressure, salinity, and low pH, extremophiles including thermophiles, barophiles, halophiles, and acidophiles can still form resilient biofilms and contribute to corrosion and biofouling. This review summarizes recent advances in understanding the formation, adaptation, and persistence of microbial biofilms in extreme environments and their roles in MIC. Key corrosion mechanisms such as extracellular electron transfer-MIC (EET-MIC) and metabolite-MIC (M-MIC) are discussed with environmental stressors and microbial physiology. Existing studies reveal that extreme environmental conditions do not necessarily suppress MIC, as extremophiles can adapt to environmental stresses and maintain corrosive activities. Different environmental stressors affect MIC through various pathways such as microbial metabolism and corrosion kinetics. Representative case studies highlight MIC behaviors under deep-sea, geothermal, hypersaline, and acidic conditions that are relevant to industrial operations. items.t: Thermophilic Parageobacillus toebii G12 suppresses ARG enrichment during chicken manure composting even with multidrug-resistant plasmid-harboring bacteria as a stressor.
items.ab: The enrichment of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) during composting poses a substantial risk to the safe utilization of chicken manure. However, the role of multidrug-resistant plasmid (MRP)-harboring bacteria in ARG dissemination and microbial succession during composting remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the regulatory effects of thermophilic Parageobacillus toebii G12 (G12) on ARG dynamics, as well as its performance under interference from MRP-harboring bacteria. Our results showed that G12 inoculation elevated compost temperature, extended the thermophilic phase, and accelerated maturation. It increased overall ARG removal to 60.9 % and 55.6 % in the conventional and MRP-contaminated systems, respectively, and reduced persistent ARG enrichment by 71.4 % and 66.3 %, respectively. Although MRP-associated stress shifted the suppression preference of G12 from protection-type to alteration/replacement-type persistent ARGs, the strain consistently suppressed efflux- and inactivation-type persistent ARGs. Moreover, G12 markedly reduced the coverage depth of MRPs after composting, thereby alleviating MRP-associated stress. items.t: Diagnostic value of metagenomic next-generation sequencing for bacterial and fungal detection and its role in antimicrobial therapy adjustment in critically ill patients with non-resolving pneumonia.
items.ab: INTRODUCTION: Early targeted antibiotic therapy is critical for improving outcomes in ICU patients with pneumonia unresponsive to initial treatment. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) is a unique diagnostic tool; however, its effectiveness for high-risk populations remains unclear. METHODS: This retrospective study included 642 ICU patients with pneumonia unresponsive to initial treatment, categorized into single- or repeat-test groups based on mNGS testing frequency. We analyzed the results of mNGS and conventional microbiological tests (CMTs), compared microbial detection characteristics between patients with different immune statuses, assessed the impact of repeat testing on microbial detection and treatment adjustments and evaluated its association with patient prognosis using multivariable logistic regression and propensity score matching. RESULTS: Among 642 patients, patient-level agreement between mNGS and CMTs was low (κ = 0.180, p < 0.001). First bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF)-mNGS results showed a higher microbial detection rate in immunocompromised than immunocompetent patients. Among patients undergoing repeat BALF-mNGS testing, partial concordance between first and second tests was most common pattern. Antibiotic treatments were modified in 67.6% of cases based on mNGS results, with a higher adjustment rate in the repeat-test group.
